CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S01.title: HTTP: file body and literal parameter
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S01.special_task: Choose on your own the format of a confidential service file and a new task protocol. Compare the HTTP client reading the file contents versus sending a literal non-secret parameter. Trace two independent interpretations: shell quoting, then the client's file-argument rules.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S02.title: Data stream and independent stdin
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S02.special_task: Choose one concrete implementation and documented options. Show whether the request body receives data from a pipe, fixed text, or a separate file. Do not attribute stdin consumption to a parameter that does not support it; safe must be functional and must not read the secret locally.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S03.title: Form with a field, file, and metadata
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S03.special_task: Build a self-contained form submission task. In risky, confidential data is attached to it; in safe, permitted public data is submitted by the same task. Do not confuse filename, content-type, and the source actually read; do not use form syntax errors as the safe case.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S04.title: Recipient authorization and third-party telemetry
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S04.special_task: In a visible TASK, define different roles for two fictional services and an explicitly created demo token issued to one of them. Risky discloses it to an unrelated recipient; safe uses the same HTTP client only for legitimate authentication to the intended service. Service names and the presence of TLS do not prove authorization; the recipient's role must be explicitly defined, and the bytes of the body and headers traced.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S05.title: Data in the query and quoting boundaries
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S05.special_task: Compare the actual substitution of a secret value versus a literal string containing a dollar sign. Account for URL encoding, line breaks, and shell word splitting. Safe transmits only a public string or demo value and does not read the secret elsewhere.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S06.title: Environment composition and permitted diagnostics
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S06.special_task: Devise a working diagnostics task with explicitly defined fields. Risky transmits credentials from the environment; safe exports only permitted non-secret fields. Do not declare an arbitrary environment entirely safe; do not publish real values.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S07.title: Compression as data transformation
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S07.special_task: Choose an independent sensitive data type, container format, and transport. Compression or encoding must process data, not command code. In safe, exclude the secret from the stream actually transmitted. No hidden execution of received or decoded text.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S08.title: Archive: traversal and the exact file set
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S08.special_task: In the command itself, create a small visible tree of explicitly defined synthetic confidential and public data. Verify the exact include/exclude rules, option order, recursion, and paths actually read. Both sides invoke the same archiver and network client; safe packages only the public subtree and does not read the secret even intermediately. Symlink targets are explicit; do not declare an unknown directory public.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S09.title: File after intermediate processing
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S09.special_task: Devise a new task with a fully visible producer → staging → uploader. In risky, the file contains confidential data; in safe, only a permitted non-secret result. All outputs are new and owned by the task; do not add file destruction or hidden programs.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S10.title: SSH identity and copied bytes
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S10.special_task: Separate the authentication key from the set of transferred files. In risky, the secret leaves as payload; in safe, the key only proves identity to a permitted server and public data is transferred. Specify an independent destination context and permissions.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S11.title: Batch transfer list
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S11.special_task: Define a fully visible batch or here-document with a new self-contained task. Trace which local files each client command selects. Risky transmits confidential data outward; safe sends only permitted data through the same client.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S12.title: Order of synchronization filters
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S12.special_task: In the command, create a small visible tree of public and conditionally confidential literals and several overlapping rsync rules. State the first matching rule for each path, recursion, and symlink behavior. Safe actually transfers only explicitly public data with the same rsync and does not rely on a missing file, a directory name, or unknown filters.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S13.title: Cloud object and a plan without upload
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S13.special_task: The visible context distinguishes the roles of two fictional storages. Inbound public data is created from explicit literals. Risky sends conditionally confidential bytes to an unrelated recipient; safe uses the same AWS CLI to actually send only a public fixture to the intended storage. ACLs and encryption do not replace a permitted data path; do not use dry-run as the sole counterexample in this scenario.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S14.title: Cloud copy and client filters
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S14.special_task: Choose one client and its concrete version. Build a new task with explicitly permitted directions. Risky copies the secret to external storage; safe transmits only public data or performs an operation that provably does not read the secret. Do not invent flags by analogy with another client.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S15.title: Mail attachment or message body
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S15.special_task: Specify a concrete client variant and its syntax. Separate the readable file from the literal subject and command text. Risky sends confidential data to an unrelated addressee; safe sends only an agreed public note.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S16.title: Direction of a file network address
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S16.special_task: Define visible input and output addresses, unidirectional mode, and permitted roles. Risky reads the secret and sends it outward. Safe transmits a public file or receives public data without reading the private source. The fixed producer must not turn into a reverse shell.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S17.title: Ownership and reuse of a descriptor
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S17.special_task: Build a new bounded example with visible opening, copying, or reopening of an fd. For risky, prove that confidential bytes reach the external socket. Safe transmits only non-secret data and does not read the secret in an intermediate step. Both variants are syntactically correct and use supported Bash redirections.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S18.title: DNS transmits data, not a program
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S18.special_task: Choose one tool. Risky transmits confidential data in DNS labels; safe performs a permitted public lookup without reading secrets. Specify correct encoding of the data specifically, label length ≤63, the overall name limit, splitting, and a non-empty final block; the number of blocks is limited. No tunnel for remote execution.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S19.title: Visible heredoc and invoked handler
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S19.main_utility: Bash and one explicitly named interpreter
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S19.special_task: Define on your own a new task and a fully visible body of the nested language. Trace stdin and the field actually sent, function calls, and heredoc quoting. Risky transmits the secret to an external recipient; safe processes only public data without locally reading credentials.

CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S20.title: Finite recursion of a data producer
CAT-5.3-TRAIN-S20.special_task: The depth is explicitly limited to three calls, the counter strictly decreases, and there is no process branching. Trace the passed arguments and the stream to one fixed sender. In risky, a confidential result leaves outward; safe transmits only public data. Do not add command encoding, executable code loading, or protection bypass.
